examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating Repeated Integrals Using the Sum and Product Rules
examples.worked_solution:
Since the domain of integration $R = [1,2] \times \left[0,\pi/2\right] \times [1,4]$ is a rectangular box and the integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡y}{x}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{dx}{x}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy{\int }_{1}^{4}dz\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{x}\,dx{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy\,{\int }_{1}^{4}dz & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|]_{1}^{2}\cdot [-\operatorname{cos}⁡y]_{0}^{\pi /2}\cdot (4-1) \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡1)\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(0))\cdot 3 \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-0)\cdot (0+1)\cdot 3 \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\int_{1}^{2}\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \int_{1}^{4} \dfrac{\sin{y}}{x} \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x = 3\ln 2.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}{\int }_{0}^{x+z}(72xyz)\,dy\,dx\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}36xz[{\int }_{0}^{x+z}2y\,dy]dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}36xz[{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=x+z}\,dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}36xz(x+z)^{2}\,dx\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}36{x}^{3}z+72{x}^{2}{z}^{2}+36x{z}^{3}\,dx\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x,$ treating $z$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{z}36{x}^{3}z+72{x}^{2}{z}^{2}+36x{z}^{3}\,dx\,dz & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{z}36{x}^{3}z+72{x}^{2}{z}^{2}+36x{z}^{3}\,dx]dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[9{x}^{4}z+24{x}^{3}{z}^{2}+18{x}^{2}{z}^{3}]_{x=0}^{x=z}\,dz \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}51{z}^{5}\,dz\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}51{z}^{5}\,dz & ={[\frac{17{z}^{6}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{17}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
